findings.title: Default-on fused-CE forward wrapper silently drops Cohere logit_scale / Granite logits_scaling / Gemma2 final_logit_softcapping on its non-fused branch
findings.claim:
c0f95ced (#988 'activate fused loss-only cross-entropy') flipped `fused_linear_cross_entropy` from opt-in to default-on: `_factory.py:374-376` now does `enable_fused_linear_ce = kwargs.get('fused_linear_cross_entropy'); if enable_fused_linear_ce is None: enable_fused_linear_ce = performance`, and `_dp_trainer.py:844-850` always passes `performance=True`. Previously the gate was `kwargs.get('fused_linear_cross_entropy', False)` (git show c0f95ced), so the wrapper was never installed unless explicitly requested. The wrapper replaces the model's own `forward`. When its fused branch is declined it falls through to its own re-implementation of the HF tail:
```python
logits = self.lm_head(hidden_states[:, slice_indices, :])
loss = self.loss_function(logits, labels, self.vocab_size, **kwargs)
```
This omits the post-`lm_head` transform that the upstream HF `forward` applies for five of the seventeen families listed in `_FUSED_CE_CAUSAL_LM`: Cohere/Cohere2 `logits = logits * self.logit_scale` (transformers/models/cohere/modeling_cohere.py:503), Granite `logits = logits / self.config.logits_scaling` (granite/modeling_granite.py:497), Gemma2/Gemma3 `final_logit_softcapping` tanh (gemma2/modeling_gemma2.py:527-530). The fused branch handles them correctly (it threads `logit_scale` and `softcap` into the kernels, cross_entropy.py:312-323); only the fallback branch is wrong.
findings.failure_scenario: DPTrainer DP-SFT of a Cohere / Command-R, Granite, or Gemma2 checkpoint on a CUDA GPU with the default `bf16=False` (`_training_arguments.py:415`, `_setup_precision` sets `_amp_dtype=None`). The trainer sets `loss_only=True` (`_dp_trainer.py:2442`) because `_fused_forward_uses_marker` is True by default, but `use_fused_ce` requires `hidden_states.is_cuda and hidden_states.dtype in (bfloat16, float16)`; fp32 hidden states on CUDA fail that test, so the else branch runs and every per-example loss and gradient is computed on untransformed logits. Measured on CPU (forcing the same branch with `shift_labels`, which `_fused_linear_ce_loss_is_supported` also rejects and which is device-independent): Cohere loss 4.92499 vs HF 4.16748 (18.2% error), Granite 4.35990 vs 4.16075 (4.8%), with the fused branch matching HF exactly. For Cohere logit_scale=0.0625 the loss is computed on logits 16x too large, producing a near-one-hot softmax and gradients for a different objective. No exception, no warning; DP clipping and noise still apply, so the run looks healthy.
evidence: packages/opaque-patches/src/opaque/api/patches/transformers/components/cross_entropy.py:356-364 - the else branch: `logits = self.lm_head(hidden_states[:, slice_indices, :])` then `loss = self.loss_function(logits, labels, self.vocab_size, **kwargs)`, with no logit_scale / logits_scaling / softcapping.

packages/opaque-patches/src/opaque/api/patches/transformers/components/cross_entropy.py:282-292 - `use_fused_ce = loss_only and _fused_linear_ce_loss_is_supported(...) and ((hidden_states.is_cuda and hidden_states.dtype in (torch.bfloat16, torch.float16)) or not hidden_states.is_cuda)` - CUDA + fp32 falls through.

packages/opaque-patches/src/opaque/api/patches/transformers/components/cross_entropy.py:151-172 - `_fused_linear_ce_loss_is_supported` also returns False for `logits_to_keep != 0`, `shift_labels`, class `weight`, tensor `ignore_index`; those routes hit the else branch on ANY device, CPU included.

packages/opaque-patches/src/opaque/api/patches/transformers/_factory.py:374-376 - new default-on gate; `git show c0f95ced -- .../_factory.py` shows the old `kwargs.get("fused_linear_cross_entropy", False)` and the removed docstring line 'fused_linear_cross_entropy defaults to False'.

packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_dp_trainer.py:844-850 (performance=True), :866-875 (_fused_forward_uses_marker), :2437-2442 (`inputs = {**inputs, "loss_only": True}`).
packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_training_arguments.py:415 - `bf16: bool = False`; _dp_trainer.py:904 `self._amp_dtype = torch.bfloat16 if a.bf16 else None`.
.venv/.../transformers/models/cohere/modeling_cohere.py:502-507, cohere2:480-485, granite:496-501, gemma2:526-534 - the transform lives in ForCausalLM.forward, not in loss_function.

Executed repro /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-opaque/2c6b9515-9455-539f-b005-ebecde2ecc66/scratchpad/work/t9_scale.py (CPU, transformers 5.15.1): cohere fused=4.16748 else=4.92499 HF-ref=4.16748 (18.18% err); granite fused=4.16075 else=4.35990 HF-ref=4.16075 (4.79% err); gemma2 0.02% err at small logits. `inspect.signature(m.forward).parameters` confirms the wrapper is installed by plain `apply_model_patches(m)` with no kwargs.
findings.fix_sketch: In the else branch, do not re-implement the HF tail. Either (a) delegate to `original(self, ...)` when `use_fused_ce` is False - the wrapper already does exactly that for `labels is None or not loss_only` at :204-220 and for MoE router logits at :225-244 - or (b) if logits must still be produced locally, apply the same `logit_scale`/`logits_scaling`/`final_logit_softcapping` that the fused branch computes at :312-323 before calling `self.loss_function`. Add a parity test per affected family that forces the fallback branch (e.g. via `shift_labels=`) and asserts the loss equals the unpatched model's loss.

findings.title: The multi-output `apply` override added by #987 breaks `torch.func.grad` without an enclosing `vmap` for both linear-CE kernels
findings.line: 278-281 (apply override) and 330 (`_, lse, token_weight = output`); same pattern at linear_cross_entropy.py:1005-1008 and :1061
findings.claim:
a839782e (#987 'reuse fused cross-entropy statistics') changed both linear-CE autograd Functions to return four/three outputs and added a classmethod override that hides the extras:
```python
@classmethod
def apply(cls, *args):
    return super().apply(*args)[0]
```
Under the functorch Grad transform, `custom_function_call_grad` builds a single-level `Generated` function whose `forward` re-enters `custom_function_call(autograd_function, ...)` at the level below (torch/_functorch/autograd_function.py:106-145). With no vmap level left, that lands on the overridden `apply`, which returns only `output[0]`. `Generated.setup_context` then hands that single tensor to `_ChunkedLinearCE.setup_context`, where `_, lse, token_weight = output` tries to unpack the loss vector, raising `ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 3)`. `vmap(grad(...))` survives only because the intermediate vmap level intercepts the re-entry; plain `.backward()` survives because it never re-enters `apply`. The identical override and unpack exist in the Triton class (`linear_cross_entropy.py:1005-1008`, `:1061` `_, lse, saved_valids, token_weight = output`), so the CUDA path has the same break.
findings.failure_scenario: `opaque.auditing.gradient_scores` computes per-canary gradient norms with a bare `grad_fn = torch.func.grad(loss_fn)` called once per example (`packages/opaque-auditing/src/opaque/api/auditing/attacks/_gradient.py:144,159`). Any `loss_fn` that runs a patched HF causal LM with `loss_only=True`, or that calls `opaque.alignment`'s documented per-example `fused_nll_loss`, now raises ValueError instead of returning a gradient, so the gradient-based privacy audit cannot run at all against a model using the fused LM-head loss. Same for any user code following the `torch.func.grad` examples in `opaque.functional`.
evidence: Executed /tmp/.../work/t3_dbg.py: `grad(0)` and `grad((0,1))` over `linear_cross_entropy_chunked` FAIL with `ValueError too many values to unpack (expected 3)`; `vmap(grad(0))` and `vmap(grad((0,1)))` are OK.
Executed /tmp/.../work/t4_old.py against `git show a839782e^:.../_linear_ce_chunked.py`: PRE-#987 both `grad(0)` and `vmap(grad(0))` are OK - this is a regression introduced by the perf commit.

Executed /tmp/.../work/t11_baregrad_model.py: a real `LlamaForCausalLM` + `apply_runtime_patches()/apply_model_patches()` + `make_functional`, `grad(loss_fn)(params, ids[0:1], labels[0:1])` with `loss_only=True` -> `FAIL ... ValueError too many values to unpack (expected 3)`, while `vmap(grad(...))` is OK.
Executed /tmp/.../work/t12_align.py: `opaque.api.alignment.sft.loss._nll.fused_nll_loss` (documented 'per-example' helper) -> `grad` FAILS, `vmap(grad)` OK, on CPU through the chunked path.
Traceback terminates at packages/opaque-patches/src/opaque/api/patches/kernels/_linear_ce_chunked.py:330 inside torch/_functorch/autograd_function.py:146 `setup_context`.

packages/opaque-patches/tests/kernels/test_linear_ce_chunked.py and test_linear_cross_entropy.py only exercise `vmap(grad(...))` and plain autograd; no test calls bare `grad`, which is why the regression landed.
findings.fix_sketch: Stop overriding `apply`. Return the tuple from `apply` and unpack at the (three) call sites, or make `setup_context` tolerant: `outputs = output if isinstance(output, tuple) else (output,)` is not enough because the aux tensors are genuinely missing at that level. The robust fix is to keep the Function single-output and pass `lse`/`valids`/`token_weight` to the backward through `ctx` fields computed in `forward` (they are all `mark_non_differentiable` anyway), or to wrap the tuple-returning Function in a plain Python function that does the `[0]`. Add a `grad(...)`-without-vmap test to both kernel test modules and to `opaque-auditing`.

findings.title: `_can_use_native_gqa`'s functorch guard never fires on the DP-SGD transform: `is_batchedtensor` is False under `vmap(grad(...))`
findings.claim: b9fb8674 (#985) added `if query.device.type != 'cuda' or torch._C._functorch.is_batchedtensor(query): return False` to keep the native `enable_gqa=True` SDPA (and its `torch.backends.cuda.SDPAParams` probe) away from functorch-wrapped tensors. Under `vmap(grad(f))` - the transform `clipped_grad`/`clipped_fun` actually uses - the tensor reaching the attention forward is a GradTrackingTensor wrapping a BatchedTensor, and `is_batchedtensor` inspects only the outermost wrapper, so it returns False. The repo already knows about this nesting: `_linear_ce_chunked._vmap_batch_factor` (lines 88-103) explicitly loops `is_gradtrackingtensor -> get_unwrapped -> is_batchedtensor`. The guard is masked on CPU by the `device.type != 'cuda'` clause, which is why no test catches it (`test_attention.py:192-201` only checks the positive CUDA case with plain tensors).
findings.failure_scenario: On CUDA, a DP-SGD step under `vmap(grad(...))` reaches `_can_use_native_gqa` with a GradTrackingTensor. The guard passes, `torch.backends.cuda.SDPAParams(query, key, value, ...)` is constructed from a functorch wrapper, and if `can_use_flash_attention` returns True the code calls `F.scaled_dot_product_attention(..., enable_gqa=True)` inside vmap - the exact path the guard was written to avoid. Best case the functorch batching fallback loops per sample (correct but slower than the `_grouped_sdpa` path that was written for it, defeating #985's purpose); worst case SDPAParams reads wrapper geometry and the eligibility decision is made on the wrong shapes/strides. Not reproducible here (no CUDA device), so only the guard's ineffectiveness is proven.
evidence: packages/opaque-patches/src/opaque/api/patches/transformers/components/attention.py:124 - `if query.device.type != "cuda" or torch._C._functorch.is_batchedtensor(query): return False`.

Executed /tmp/.../work/t7_bt.py: under `vmap(lambda a: ...)` -> is_batched=True, is_gradtrack=False; under `vmap(grad(...))` -> **is_batched=False**, is_gradtrack=True; under `grad(...)` -> is_batched=False, is_gradtrack=True.

packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/clipping/_clipped_grad.py:283 `grad_and_value(...)` wrapped by `_clipped_fun.py:595,682 _vmap(...)` - the DP path is vmap-outside-grad, so the inner tensors are grad-tracking wrappers.
packages/opaque-patches/src/opaque/api/patches/kernels/_linear_ce_chunked.py:88-103 - the correct two-level unwrap idiom already present in the same package.
packages/opaque-patches/tests/transformers/components/test_attention.py:192-201 - the only eligibility test uses plain CUDA tensors; no test asserts the guard rejects a functorch-wrapped query.
findings.fix_sketch: Replace the single-level check with the same unwrap loop used by `_vmap_batch_factor`, or simply test both predicates: `f = torch._C._functorch; if f.is_batchedtensor(query) or f.is_gradtrackingtensor(query): return False`. Add a CPU-runnable unit test that monkeypatches the device check and asserts `_can_use_native_gqa` returns False inside `vmap(grad(...))`.

findings.title: RMSNorm / fused-add-RMSNorm / RoPE backwards overwrite the upstream gradient buffer on a single backward, not only on a repeated one (wider than tracked #898)
findings.line: 557 (`dX = dY if in_place else torch.zeros_like(dY)`); fused_add_rms_norm.py:322; rope_embedding.py:237-238, 455-458; components/rms_norm.py:35,41 (`in_place_bwd=True`)
findings.claim: Tracked issue #898 ('Audit remaining fused kernels for repeated-backward gap') is scoped to *repeated* backward through fused activations, which #874 addressed by adding `ctx._opaque_backward_done` to SwiGLU/GeGLU/LoRA_MLP. The RMSNorm family and RoPE have a different and wider aliasing: their backward writes the input gradient directly into the *upstream* gradient tensor on the FIRST backward. `_rms_norm_backward_triton` does `dX = dY if in_place else torch.zeros_like(dY)` after `dY = dY.contiguous().view(-1, dim)` - `.contiguous()` is identity for an already-contiguous grad, so `dX` aliases the caller's tensor. The default Llama and Gemma RMSNorm component patches enable this (`components/rms_norm.py:35,41` pass `in_place_bwd=True`). `_RoPEBackward.forward` and `_RoPE_QK_Backward.forward` do the same with the comment 'In-place: overwrite grad_Q buffer (internal gradient, safe to mutate)'. #943, which removed the forward's Q/K clones, deliberately left the backward aliasing in place (it passes `dQ, dQ.stride(0), dQ, dQ.stride(0)` as both in and out pointers).
findings.failure_scenario: `torch.autograd.grad(y, x, grad_outputs=g)` (or `y.backward(gradient=g)`) where the RMSNorm/RoPE node is the first node the engine visits: the engine hands the caller's `g` to that backward unchanged, the Triton kernel overwrites it, and `g` is silently different afterwards. A caller that reuses `g` for a second `torch.autograd.grad` call, or that inspects it (e.g. an auditing or gradient-probe harness that keeps its seed vector), gets numbers derived from already-transformed data. Triton stores bypass the dispatcher so the version counter is not bumped and autograd raises nothing. Not executable here (Triton path is CUDA-only, `torch.cuda.is_available()` is False), so this is a static finding; the aliasing itself is unambiguous from the code.
evidence: packages/opaque-patches/src/opaque/api/patches/kernels/rms_norm.py:533 `dY = dY.contiguous().view(-1, dim)` and :557 `dX = dY if in_place else torch.zeros_like(dY)`.
packages/opaque-patches/src/opaque/api/patches/kernels/fused_add_rms_norm.py:322 `dX = dY if in_place else torch.empty_like(dY)`.

packages/opaque-patches/src/opaque/api/patches/transformers/components/rms_norm.py:35,41 - `in_place_bwd=True` for the default llama and gemma RMSNorm patches (only the 'lite'/gemma3 variants at :47,55,61 use False).

packages/opaque-patches/src/opaque/api/patches/kernels/rope_embedding.py:236-238 `dQ = grad_Q.reshape(...).contiguous()` with the 'safe to mutate' comment, and :262-266 passing `dQ` as both input and output pointer; :455-458 the same for `dQ_out`/`dK_out`.
git show 26f6247b - #943 replaced `Q.clone()` with `torch.empty_like(Q)` in the forwards only; the backward launches still alias in and out.
Guarded classes per grep: only geglu.py:249/515, swiglu.py:251, lora.py:1120 carry `_opaque_backward_done`; rms_norm, fused_add_rms_norm, rope_embedding, moe have none.
findings.fix_sketch: Either document `in_place_bwd`/RoPE backward as taking ownership of the incoming grad and default the component patches to `in_place_bwd=False`, or allocate the output buffer when `torch.is_grad_enabled()` / when the incoming grad is not uniquely owned. Minimum: extend tracked issue #898's scope from 'repeated backward' to 'upstream-gradient aliasing on the first backward', and add a CUDA test that calls `torch.autograd.grad(y, x, grad_outputs=g)` and asserts `g` is unchanged (mirroring the `torch.testing.assert_close(Q_op, Q_before, rtol=0, atol=0)` forward checks #943 already added).

clean_areas: Chunked portable linear CE (`_linear_ce_chunked.py`, rewritten by #990/#988/#987/#980/#978) - numerical parity: ran every feature combination (plain, label_smoothing=0.2/0.3, logit_softcapping=3/5, logit_scale=0.25/0.5, use_token_scaling, and combinations) at float64 against an independent `logits -> F.cross_entropy` reference, for chunk_vocab in {None, 4, 1}, with ignore_index positions including one sample whose labels are ALL -100. Loss, d_hidden and d_weight all agree to <= 7.1e-15 absolute. Label smoothing matches the HF identity (1-eps)*nll + eps*(lse - mean_v z_v) and its gradient p_j - eps/V - (1-eps)*1{j=t} sums to zero over the vocabulary. (work/t1_chunked.py)

Chunked linear CE per-sample isolation under `vmap(grad(...))` - compared `vmap(grad(loss))` against an explicit per-sample loop for grads w.r.t. both hidden states and the (shared) LM head, at float64, chunk_vocab in {None, 3}; max diff 0.0. Then perturbed sample 2's hidden states by +3.0 and re-ran: samples 0, 1, 3 gradients changed by exactly 0.0 (dh and dw), i.e. no cross-sample leakage through the streamed LSE, the token/vocab tiling, or the `torch.cat`-based accumulators. (work/t2_vmap.py)

Chunked linear CE mixed/low precision (#980's deliberate change from fp32-upcast to eager-precision linear) - verified the new `_linear_chunk` rounds bf16xbf16 logits to bf16 before promoting, which matches the Triton kernel's `accum.cast(E.dtype.element_ty, fp_downcast_rounding='rtne')` at linear_cross_entropy.py:175 and :381 (and the backward's d_accum downcast at :417), i.e. the change improved Triton<->portable consistency rather than degrading it. Measured against eager: bf16/bf16 loss rel 8e-8, dh rel 5.7e-3 (bf16 eps), dw exact; bf16/fp32 exact; fp32/fp32 rel <= 4.5e-7. Forward and backward use the same cast boundary in every dtype combination (`cast_hidden` in `_stream_lse` vs `low_precision_linear` in `backward`). (work/t13_bf16.py)

Fused CE backward buffer separation (#931, 263c8c43) - read the Triton `_cross_entropy_backward` and both `_CrossEntropyBackward.forward` and `.vmap`: the kernel now takes a distinct `grad_logits_ptr` (indexed `row_idx.to(tl.int64) * VOCAB_SIZE`, int64-safe) and writes only there, while saved `logits` are read-only via `logits_row_stride`. `grad_logits = torch.empty_like(logits, memory_format=torch.contiguous_format)` guarantees the assumed row stride. This is strictly safer than the clone it replaced, and the commit added non-mutation assertions for both the plain and vmapped paths.

LoRA MLP saved-activation mutation (OPQ-343 root cause) is structurally gone after #934 - `Opaque_LoRA_MLP.setup_context` (lora.py:1100-1118) now saves only X and the weights, and `backward` (lora.py:1133-1142) recomputes `gate`/`up` locally before handing them to the in-place activation backward. The `gate`/`up` values returned as forward outputs are therefore no longer the buffers the Triton kernel overwrites. #953's `_ACTIVATION_BACKWARD_LITE` path mutates the same freshly recomputed locals. The `_opaque_backward_done` guard from #874 is still present (lora.py:1120-1122) and is now conservative rather than necessary.

Fused add/RMSNorm RSTD reuse (#944, ab56b590) - the removed `S.detach().clone()` is safe: grepped every `tl.store` in fused_add_rms_norm.py (lines 100, 117, 129, 213, 216) and the backward kernel writes only to `dx_base` and `dW_ptr`; `S` is a pure read. Saving the live output instead of a clone additionally restores version-counter protection. The reused RSTD is `rsqrt(mean(S^2)+eps)` computed inside the forward kernel in the casting-mode's own precision (fp32 for modes 0/1, input dtype for -1), which is the same formula the deleted `_torch_rstd` used and is now forward/backward-consistent by construction. Output arity went 2->3 and all four call sites in components/fused_add_rms_norm.py (:58,110,163,216) plus the public wrapper unpack three.

RMSNorm HAS_WEIGHT / COMPUTE_DW split (#984, 2caf3aab) - verified the two flags are used independently in `_rms_norm_backward_kernel`, so a frozen-but-present weight still multiplies into dX while skipping the dW accumulator; `dW_ptr = _dW if _dW is not None else dY` is never written because COMPUTE_DW is a constexpr False. The new per-sample `_rms_norm_weight_grad_partial_kernel` uses the identical accumulation expression as the fused kernel in both casting modes, correctly excludes `offset` from dW, and its chunking (`n_chunks = min(rows, ceil(sm/B))`, `rows_per_program = ceil(rows/n_chunks)`, `row_end = min(...)`) covers every row exactly once. In `_RMSNormBackward.vmap` the per-sample dW is computed BEFORE the in-place `_rms_norm_backward_triton` overwrites dY - the ordering that makes `in_place` safe there.

`ctx.compute_dw = W is not None and W.requires_grad` (rms_norm.py:731) and `_needs_lora_weight_grads` (lora.py:89-93) - empirically confirmed the requires_grad probe is sound under the DP transform: inside `vmap(grad(f, (0,1)))` the differentiated weight arrives at `setup_context` with `requires_grad == True` and `ctx.needs_input_grad == (True, True)`, while a non-differentiated captured weight shows False. So a trainable norm weight never silently loses its gradient. (work/t5_reqgrad.py)

`Opaque_RMSNorm` returning `X2d` (a view of its own input) as a third, `mark_non_differentiable` output - reproduced the pattern on CPU with a mock Function: the output aliases the input storage, `requires_grad` stays True (mark_non_differentiable does not sever the view relationship), and gradients to both X and W are bit-identical to the eager reference. No correctness issue. (work/t10_viewout.py)

GQA K/V replication removal (#985, b9fb8674) - exact parity on CPU at float64 between `_grouped_sdpa` / `_grouped_eager_attention` and a `vmap_repeat_kv`-based reference: max |diff| = 0.0 for attn_mask in {None, float (B,1,Q,K), float (B,H_q,Q,K), bool (B,1,Q,K)} and for `is_causal=True`; eager attention weights also 0.0. Verified the head-order contract matches HF `repeat_kv` (kv head j serves query heads [j*G, (j+1)*G)), that `_kv_group`'s `expand` gives stride-0 views whose backward sums correctly, and that `vmap(grad(...))` per-sample gradients w.r.t. q, k and v match the replicated reference to 0.0. Also checked `vmap_sdpa_attention_forward` reproduces HF 5.15's `sdpa_attention_forward` control flow (is_causal derivation, prefill key/value slicing, `create_position_bias_mask`). (work/t6_gqa.py)

Triton fused linear-CE shifted-index translation (#945) - hand-checked `source_offs_b = offs_b + offs_b // tokens_per_sequence` in both the forward (linear_cross_entropy.py:148) and backward (:354) kernels: for logical token b it resolves to seq*(T+1)+off with target at +1, so no read ever crosses a sequence boundary into the next sample's hidden states or labels - the specific cross-sample leak the copy-free shift could have introduced. Also checked the valids round-trip `_saved_valids`/`_restore_valids` distinguishes 'all tokens valid' (empty tensor + lse.numel()==n_tokens) from 'all tokens ignored' (empty tensor + lse.numel()==0), and that per-sample dC bucketing `sample_ids = offs_b // tokens_per_sample` uses the logical (not valids-compacted) position while `lse` is read at the compacted index.

Test-weakening sweep across the delta - diffed every `rtol`/`atol`/`skip`/`xfail` line in `packages/opaque-patches/tests`: no tolerance was widened on an existing assertion. The only `pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(not torch.cuda.is_available())` change REMOVES a skip (tests/peft/test_fused_lora_qkv.py), making the QKV-fusion routing tests run on CPU. New assertions added by the perf commits include exact non-mutation checks (`rtol=0, atol=0`) on forward inputs for RoPE, RMSNorm and LoRA. The full CPU-selectable patches suite passes: 405 passed, 142 skipped, 310 deselected.

Not reported as new findings because they duplicate tracked work: #898 (repeated-backward gap in remaining fused kernels) - the SwiGLU/GeGLU `_opaque_backward_done` guards from #874 cover only three classes and rms_norm/fused_add_rms_norm/rope_embedding/moe still have none; #880 (CUDA marker coverage for LoRA and linear-CE kernel tests); #958/#963 (SDPA batching and sliding-window perf).
